concepts.title: Place Value: Tens and Ones
concepts.description: Understanding that in a two-digit number, digits represent different values based on their position (tens place and ones place).
key_ideas: Grouping objects into bundles of ten
Identifying the digit in the tens place versus the ones place
Visualizing numbers using base-10 blocks or bundles

concepts.title: Expanded Form of Numbers
concepts.description: Expressing a number as the sum of the values of its digits to understand its composition.
key_ideas: Writing numbers as a sum (e.g., 45 = 40 + 5)
Connecting expanded form to spoken number names
Decomposing numbers into tens and ones

concepts.title: Number Names and Writing
concepts.description: Reading and writing the number names (words) for numerals up to 100.
key_ideas: Spelling number words (e.g., 'Twenty', 'Thirty')
Matching numerals to their written word form
Hyphenating compound numbers (e.g., 'Twenty-one')

concepts.description: Counting forward by numbers other than one to identify patterns and prepare for multiplication.

Identifying patterns on a 100-chart
Completing number sequences with gaps

concepts.title: Ordinal Numbers
concepts.description: Using numbers to define the position or rank of an object in a sequence.
key_ideas: Distinguishing between cardinal (counting) and ordinal (position) numbers
Using terms like 1st, 2nd, 3rd, up to 10th or 20th
Identifying the position of items in a line

Step-by-step problem solving for word problems on addition and subtraction

concepts.title: Properties of Addition and Subtraction
concepts.description: Understanding fundamental rules like the order of numbers in addition and the effect of zero.
key_ideas: Changing the order of addends does not change the sum (Commutative Property)
Adding zero to a number gives the same number
Subtracting zero from a number leaves the number unchanged

concepts.title: Adding Three One-Digit Numbers
concepts.description: Learning strategies to add three distinct single-digit numbers together by grouping them efficiently.
key_ideas: Grouping two numbers that make 10 first
Adding numbers vertically in a column
Keeping a running total in your head

concepts.title: Addition with Regrouping (Carry Over)
concepts.description: Solving addition problems where the sum of the digits in the ones place exceeds 9, requiring carrying over to the tens place.
key_ideas: Identifying when a sum is greater than 9
Carrying the 'tens' digit to the next column
Adding the carried digit to the tens column numbers

concepts.title: Subtraction with Borrowing
concepts.description: Solving subtraction problems where the digit in the ones place of the minuend is smaller than the subtrahend.
key_ideas: Recognizing when the top digit is smaller than the bottom digit
Borrowing 1 ten from the tens place and converting it to 10 ones
Reducing the tens count by one after borrowing

concepts.title: Relationship Between Addition and Subtraction
concepts.description: Understanding how addition and subtraction are inverse operations through fact families.
key_ideas: If A + B = C, then C - B = A
Using addition to check subtraction answers
Creating fact families (e.g., 3, 5, 8 creates 3+5=8 and 8-5=3)

concepts.title: Straight and Curved Lines
concepts.description: Introduction to different types of lines used to draw shapes, distinguishing between straight lines (standing, sleeping, slanting) and curved lines.
key_ideas: Standing lines (vertical)
Sleeping lines (horizontal)
Slanting lines (diagonal)
Curved lines vs straight lines

concepts.title: Sides and Corners
concepts.description: Analyzing basic 2D shapes by counting their straight edges (sides) and the points where edges meet (corners/vertices).
key_ideas: Counting sides of squares, rectangles, and triangles
Counting corners of shapes
Identifying shapes with zero corners (circle)
Relating the number of sides to the shape name

concepts.title: Solid Shapes Around Us
concepts.description: Identifying 3D solid shapes in everyday environment, such as balls (spheres), boxes (cuboids), and pipes (cylinders).
key_ideas: Identifying spheres (ball-like)
Identifying cuboids/cubes (box-like)
Identifying cylinders (can-like) and cones
Matching real-world objects to geometric solids

concepts.title: Rolling and Sliding
concepts.description: Determining how different objects move based on their surface properties—whether they roll, slide, or do both.
key_ideas: Curved surfaces allow rolling
Flat surfaces allow sliding
Objects with both curved and flat surfaces (like a coin or can) can do both
Predicting movement of an object

concepts.title: Tracing Flat Shapes from Solids
concepts.description: Understanding the relationship between 3D objects and 2D shapes by tracing the faces of solid objects to create flat shapes.
key_ideas: Tracing a box creates a square or rectangle
Tracing a cylinder or cone base creates a circle
Relationship between a solid's face and a 2D drawing
Creating 2D art using 3D objects

concepts.title: Measuring Length — Hand Span, Foot

concepts.title: Heavier and Lighter
concepts.description: Introduction to the concept of weight by comparing two objects to determine which is heavier and which is lighter through direct handling.
key_ideas: Understanding weight as a property of objects
Comparing two objects by lifting
Identifying heavy vs. light objects
Ordering objects from lightest to heaviest

concepts.title: Measuring with Objects
concepts.description: Measuring the length of larger items using smaller, uniform objects like erasers, matchsticks, or pencils to introduce consistency in measurement.
key_ideas: Using objects as non-standard units of measurement
Placing objects end-to-end without gaps
Counting objects to determine total length
Understanding why using the same object gives consistent results

concepts.title: Using a Balance Scale
concepts.description: Using a simple beam balance to compare weights visually and measuring weight using non-standard units like marbles or stones.
key_ideas: The heavier side of a balance goes down
The lighter side of a balance goes up
Balanced scales mean equal weight
Counting how many small units (e.g., marbles) balance a larger object

concepts.title: Measuring Liquids with Containers
concepts.description: Quantifying capacity by counting how many smaller containers (like a mug) are needed to fill a larger container (like a bucket).
key_ideas: Using a small vessel to measure a large vessel
Counting the number of pours required to fill a container
Comparing capacity: Which bucket holds more mugs of water?
Conservation of volume (pouring same water into different shapes)

concepts.title: Estimating Measurements
concepts.description: Developing the skill to guess lengths, weights, or capacities before measuring to check for reasonableness.
key_ideas: Guessing distances in steps or spans
Predicting which object is heavier before lifting
Estimating how many cups will fill a jug
Comparing the estimate with the actual measurement

concepts.title: Days of Week and Months of Year

concepts.title: Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow
concepts.description: Applying the concepts of past, present, and future to the days of the week to determine relative timing.
key_ideas: Meaning of 'Today' as the current day

Identifying the day after (Tomorrow)
Sequencing days relative to a specific event

concepts.description: Associating specific months of the year with the primary seasons (Summer, Winter, Rainy/Monsoon) observed in the region.
key_ideas: Identifying major seasons
Grouping months into seasons
Associating weather and clothing with specific times of year

concepts.title: Reading a Calendar Grid
concepts.description: Using a monthly calendar grid to locate specific dates, identify the day of the week for a given date, and count days.
key_ideas: Locating specific dates on a grid
Identifying the day of the week for a specific number
Recognizing holidays and Sundays
Counting the total number of days in a specific month

concepts.title: Estimating Time Duration
concepts.description: Comparing different activities to determine which takes a longer or shorter amount of time to complete.
key_ideas: Concept of duration (how long something takes)
Comparing 'fast' vs 'slow' activities
Estimating if an activity takes minutes, hours, or days

concepts.title: Counting Coins and Notes

Exchanging coins for notes
Grouping smaller values to match larger values

concepts.title: Adding Money Amounts

concepts.description: Determining the amount of money returned when paying with a note or coin that has a higher value than the item's cost.
key_ideas: Subtraction of money
Understanding 'change'

concepts.description: Solving real-world narrative problems involving buying items, checking affordability, and handling transactions.

concepts.title: Equal Groups — Groups of 2, 3, 5

concepts.title: Multiplication as Repeated Addition
concepts.description: Understanding that multiplication is a faster way to add the same number multiple times.
key_ideas: Connecting '3 + 3 + 3 + 3' to '4 groups of 3'
Replacing long addition sums with multiplication concepts
Identifying the number being added and how many times it is added

concepts.title: The Multiplication Symbol (x)
concepts.description: Introduction to the multiplication sign 'x' and writing multiplication sentences.
key_ideas: Recognizing the 'x' symbol as 'times'

concepts.description: Visualizing multiplication by arranging objects into equal rows and columns.

key_ideas: Identifying patterns in the 2s (doubling), 5s (ending in 0 or 5), and 10s (ending in 0)

concepts.title: One-Step Word Problems
concepts.description: Applying multiplication concepts to solve simple real-life text problems.
key_ideas: Identifying keywords like 'each', 'groups of', and 'total'
